description:
Every semantic mutation re-resolves each document reference in the repository through two fresh git subprocesses, so mutation latency scales with the repository's document-reference count rather than with the size of the change. At this repository's current size a dependency add costs 3.2 s, of which 2.3 s is process spawning.

## Background

Repository image capture backs `@/inv/derived-state-coherence`: a mutation derives its coupled materializations from one final repository view, so the capture must witness every document reference that view depends on. Capture builds that evidence one reference at a time. `capture_capability_image` iterates the pinned set and calls `inspect_pinned_target` per entry (`crates/jit/src/storage/repository_state_store.rs:888-894`), which spawns `git rev-parse --verify <rev>^{commit}` to resolve the revision (`crates/jit/src/storage/git_revision.rs:144`) and then `git ls-tree` to classify one path (`crates/jit/src/storage/git_revision.rs:208`).

Neither spawn is amortized across the set. Unpinned references all carry one revision (`UNPINNED_REVISION = "HEAD"`, `crates/jit/src/document/reference.rs:40`), and every reference in this repository is unpinned, so the revision half is a single identical query repeated once per reference. The path half asks git for one tree entry at a time where one full-tree listing answers every entry at once.

The per-reference cost is then multiplied by the capture count. A dependency add captures twice, once in preflight and once in the attempt (`crates/jit/src/commands/dependency.rs:259-310`); issue creation captures three times.

Measured on this repository at 1071 issues and 445 unpinned document references:

| operation | git processes | wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dependency add | 1575 | 3209 ms |
| issue create | 2361 | 3164 ms |
| whole-repository validate | 789 | 1087 ms |
| any read operation | 3 | 27-36 ms |

Latency is linear in two independent terms: 0.18 ms per issue, and 4.5 ms per document reference. The second dominates. Removing the document references from those same 1071 issues drops a dependency add to 203 ms, a 15.8x difference at unchanged issue count, which isolates the reference term as the cause.

Reads are unaffected and stay flat. The defect is confined to the capture path that mutations and whole-repository validation share.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Resolving a revision already resolved while serving one command issues no further git process, so a mutation over N unpinned references spawns a constant number of revision-resolution processes rather than N.
- [hard] REQ-02: Classifying N document paths at one revision issues a number of git processes independent of N.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each distinct revision-and-path pair is resolved at most once per command, however many times the repository image is captured while serving it.
- [hard] REQ-04: A dependency add over 1071 issues and 445 unpinned document references spawns fewer than 20 git processes and completes in under 1000 ms, evidenced by a benchmark artifact committed under the issue and linked to it.
- [hard] REQ-05: Pinned-document evidence is unchanged for every target class: resolved commit, object id, target kind, content identity, and unavailable reason match what per-reference resolution produces today for a present file, a directory, a path missing from the commit, and an unresolvable revision.
- [hard] REQ-06: Core commands still work with git absent, and a reference whose revision cannot be resolved still records its unavailable reason rather than failing the command.
- [hard] REQ-07: Regression coverage fails if per-reference revision resolution, per-path tree classification, or duplicate resolution across captures is reintroduced.

## Notes

The measurements come from synthetic repositories subsampled from this one, varying issue count and document-reference count independently, timed on tmpfs. Timings on tmpfs and on disk agree to within 4%, which establishes the cost as process spawning rather than storage I/O. A CPU profile attributes the remainder to `CaptureSpec::validate`, path parsing, and SHA-256 content hashing, all of which stay linear in reference count and are out of scope here.

Scaling stays linear after the fix, so the reference term governs how the tracker ages: at roughly twice the current size an unfixed mutation costs about 6 s.

`@/charter/D-4` keeps git optional for core commands, which bounds the fix: batching may not turn an absent or failing git into a hard error on a path that tolerates it today.
title: Every mutation spawns two git processes per document reference
